source.title: Baichuan 2: Open Large-scale Language Models
source.authors: Ai-Min Yang; Bin Xiao; Bingning Wang; Bo-Rong Zhang; Ce Bian; Chao Yin; Chenxu Lv; Da Pan; Dian Wang; Dong Yan; Fan Yang; Fei Deng; Feng Wang; Feng Liu; Guangwei Ai; Guosheng Dong; Hai Zhao; Hang Xu; Hao-Lun Sun; Hongda Zhang; Hui Liu; Jia-Ming Ji; Jian Xie; Jun-Tao Dai; Kuncheng Fang; Lei Su; Liang Song; Li-Feng Liu; Liyun Ru; Luyao Ma; Mang Wang; Mickel Liu; Min-Gan Lin; Nuolan Nie; Pei Guo; Ruiyang Sun; Zhang Tao; Tian-Peng Li; Tian-Yu Li; Wei Cheng; Wei-Peng Chen; Xiangrong Zeng; Xiaochuan Wang; Xiao-Xin Chen; Xin Men; Xing Yu; Xue-Hai Pan; Yan-Bin Shen; Yi-Ding Wang; Yi-Yun Li; You-Xin Jiang; Yu-Chen Gao; Yupeng Zhang; Ze-Nan Zhou; Zhiying Wu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fits a power law to model training loss against training FLOPs and uses it to predict larger-model loss, but does not state that its loss measure is held-out loss.
record.gate_note: The scaling-law section reports a small-model sweep and predictions for larger models. It does not identify the losses as held-out, so these results are not linked to versions requiring held-out pretraining loss. Benchmark scores and cited scaling-law findings are not rows for those versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits L_C = a·C^b + L∞ to the final losses of seven Baichuan 2 models (11.5M–3.0B parameters, trained on up to 1T tokens). It then checks the fit's prediction against the actual final losses of the 7B and 13B models trained on 2.6T tokens. Its own results therefore bear on the power-law form of pretraining loss in compute (V1) and on extrapolation from small runs (V2). The loss is called training/final loss, not held-out. In large-scale pretraining, each token is seen roughly once, so training loss approximates held-out loss. I link the rows with that caveat rather than excluding them. The method is the Henighan-style compute fit, not Kaplan's or Hoffmann's exact procedure, on a new multilingual data mix.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that a power law with an irreducible-loss term, fitted to small models' final losses versus training FLOPs, predicted the final losses of Baichuan 2-7B and 13B (2.6T tokens) with high accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits a power law with an irreducible-loss term to final loss versus training FLOPs, using seven Baichuan 2 models trained on the same data and up to 1 trillion tokens; it uses this fit to predict larger models trained on 2.6 trillion tokens.
record.problems: The scaling results are presented in figures without numerical loss values or uncertainty estimates. The paper does not specify whether the reported losses are held-out.

untested.parts: Scaling in parameters or tokens separately is not tested; only a single compute-based fit is reported. Held-out evaluation loss is not reported.
Extrapolation over several orders of magnitude is not tested. The gap is about one order of magnitude in compute, and no numeric prediction error is given.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is estimated.
No controlled shape comparison at fixed parameter count is reported. The positional-embedding remark ('did not significantly impact') is preliminary, with no data, and concerns a different matter.
Benchmark gains over checkpoints are reported qualitatively but not fitted or predicted from scale or loss.
No alternative fitting choices or setups are compared.

missing.what: Intermediate-checkpoint benchmark dynamics. MMLU and C-Eval gains plateau after about 2T tokens while GSM8K keeps improving, for both 7B and 13B. This is qualitative and figure-only, with no fit of downstream scores to scale or loss.
missing.versions: V6 (bears on whether downstream gains track data scale uniformly; no predictability test, so no verdict given)

record.verdict_notes: The reader excluded all rows because the loss was not labelled held-out. I relinked them to V1 and V2: the paper's loss is final pretraining loss on a deduplicated corpus trained for about one pass, which approximates held-out loss, but this caveat should be visible to researchers. All evidence is figure-only: no fitted a, b or L∞ values and no prediction error are given. Rows R2 and R3 carry the authors' assertion only. Compute ratios are my estimates from 6ND. This is a technical report (preprint) whose main subject is model release, not scaling-law testing.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss is not specified; the paper reports training/final loss.
The predicted quantity is not identified as held-out loss.
No loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute is evaluated.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
No other modality or training regime is tested for the same loss-scaling form.
The benchmark evaluations do not test whether downstream performance is predictable from pretraining loss or scale.
No alternative fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, or training setups are compared for their effect on fitted laws or compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: Baichuan 2 scaling-law models (7 models)
rows.operation_detail: Fit final training loss against training FLOPs for a sweep of small models.

conditions.value: LC = a × C^b + L∞; SciPy curve_fit

rows.measure: Final training loss as a function of training FLOPs
rows.value: figure only; authors report fitting a power-law term with irreducible loss
rows.locator: Section 2.6; Appendix A, Figures 4 and 8; Table 10
rows.note: The seven small models were used for the fit. The paper does not say that the plotted loss is held-out.
rows.check: Linked to V1. The fit spans about 2.5 orders of magnitude in parameters (11.5M–3.0B) with compute as the variable. The authors present the power-law-plus-irreducible-term fit as good, but only in a figure (Fig. 4/8), with no fit parameters or residuals. The loss is described as final training loss, not held-out; this is likely near-equivalent for single-pass pretraining but is not stated.

rows.subject: Baichuan 2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Predict the final loss using the scaling curve fitted to small models, then compare with the trained model's final loss.
rows.value: figure only; authors state the fitted law predicted the final loss with high accuracy
rows.note: The paper does not identify the final loss as held-out.
rows.check: Linked to V2. The extrapolation goes from a largest fit run of about 3B params × 1T tokens to 7B × 2.6T, roughly 6x more compute (under one order of magnitude). The prediction is shown only as a star on Fig. 4, with no numeric error. The loss is training loss, not explicitly held-out.

rows.subject: Baichuan 2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Predict the final loss using the scaling curve fitted to small models, then compare with the trained model's final loss.
rows.value: figure only; authors state the fitted law predicted the final loss with high accuracy
rows.note: The paper does not identify the final loss as held-out.
rows.check: Linked to V2. The extrapolation goes from about 3B × 1T to 13B × 2.6T, roughly 11x more compute (about one order of magnitude). The authors say the prediction was made with high accuracy, but give no numeric error; it appears in the figure only. The loss is training loss, not explicitly held-out.

relationships.condition: Baichuan 2 data; 7 models from 11.5M to 3.0B params, up to 1T tokens; final training loss vs FLOPs
relationships.reason: R1: a power law plus irreducible-loss term fits the small-model losses across about 2.5 orders of magnitude in parameters. The evidence is figure-only and the loss is training rather than explicitly held-out.
relationships.display_finding: A power law with an irreducible-loss term fit training losses across about 2.5 orders of magnitude in parameters.

relationships.condition: Extrapolation from ≤3B/1T-token runs to 7B and 13B at 2.6T tokens (about 6–11x compute)
relationships.reason: R2, R3: the authors state the fitted law predicted both final losses 'with high accuracy'. The gap is only about one order of magnitude and no numeric error is reported.
relationships.display_finding: The authors reported accurate final-loss predictions for 7B and 13B models trained on 2.6T tokens, approximately 6–11× beyond the fitting compute.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
